questions.question: Prior to India, which country introduced Five-Year Plans for policy-making purposes?

options.text: The Union of Soviet Socialist Republics

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The Union of Soviet Socialist Republics**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Union of Soviet Socialist Republics (USSR) was the first country to introduce the concept of Five-Year Plans.
 
• The USSR introduced its first Five-Year Plan in 1928 under the leadership of Joseph Stalin.
 
• The primary goal of the first Five-Year Plan was to rapidly industrialize the nation and boost its economy.
 
• The success of the Soviet Five-Year Plans influenced many other countries, including India, to adopt similar planning strategies for economic development.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Five-Year Plans**

 
 
• Five-Year Plans are centralized and integrated national economic programs.
 
• The concept was first implemented in the Soviet Union and later adopted by various other countries.
 
• These plans aim to develop sectors such as agriculture, industry, and services by setting specific targets over a five-year period.
 
• The plans are designed to achieve rapid economic development and are often associated with socialist and centrally planned economies.
 
 
 
• **Soviet Five-Year Plans**
 
 
• The first Soviet Five-Year Plan (1928-1932) focused on the rapid industrialization of the USSR, particularly in heavy industries such as steel, coal, and machinery.
 
• The plan also aimed to collectivize agriculture to increase productivity and ensure state control over food supplies.
 
• Despite initial challenges and resistance, the first plan achieved significant industrial growth and laid the foundation for future economic development.
 
• Subsequent Five-Year Plans continued to build on these achievements, with varying degrees of success and challenges.
 
 
 
• **India's Five-Year Plans**
 
 
• India adopted the concept of Five-Year Plans after gaining independence in 1947.
 
• The Planning Commission was established in 1950 to oversee the formulation and implementation of these plans.
 
• India's first Five-Year Plan (1951-1956) focused on agriculture, irrigation, and energy production to rebuild the economy after independence.
 
• India continued to implement Five-Year Plans until the Planning Commission was replaced by the NITI Aayog in 2015.

questions.question: During eighth Five year plan, India became a member of the World Trade Organization on 1 January _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1995**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• India became a member of the World Trade Organization (WTO) on 1 January 1995.
 
• The World Trade Organization (WTO) is an intergovernmental organization that regulates international trade.
 
• WTO officially commenced on 1 January 1995 under the Marrakesh Agreement, replacing the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (GATT).
 
• As a member of the WTO, India has to adhere to its rules and regulations and can benefit from the international trading system.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **World Trade Organization (WTO)**

 
 
• The WTO is the only global international organization dealing with the rules of trade between nations.
 
• Its main function is to ensure that trade flows as smoothly, predictably, and freely as possible.
 
• The WTO provides a forum for negotiating agreements aimed at reducing obstacles to international trade and ensuring a level playing field for all, thus contributing to economic growth and development.
 
• The WTO also provides a legal and institutional framework for the implementation and monitoring of these agreements, as well as for settling disputes arising from their interpretation and application.
 
 
 
• **General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (GATT)**
 
 
• The GATT was a legal agreement between many countries, whose overall purpose was to promote international trade by reducing or eliminating trade barriers such as tariffs or quotas.
 
• It was signed by 23 nations in Geneva on October 30, 1947, and took effect on January 1, 1948.
 
• The GATT was intended to boost economic recovery after World War II through reconstructing and liberalizing global trade.
 
• The GATT continued to exist until it was replaced by the WTO on January 1, 1995.
 
 
 
• **Marrakesh Agreement**
 
 
• The Marrakesh Agreement established the World Trade Organization, signed in Marrakesh, Morocco, on April 15, 1994.
 
• The agreement marked the culmination of the Uruguay Round of GATT negotiations, which lasted from 1986 to 1994.
 
• It resulted in the most significant reform of the global trading system since the GATT was created in 1948.
 
• The Marrakesh Agreement incorporated the GATT framework and expanded it to include new areas such as services and intellectual property.

questions.question: During the period of 1947 to 1990, how many five-year plans were completed?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**7**__.

• **Five-Year Plans in India**

 
 
• The Five-Year Plans were centralized and integrated national economic programs.
 
• They were modeled after the Soviet Union's centralized economic planning, aiming to promote rapid industrialization and economic development.
 
• Each plan was formulated, executed, and monitored by the Planning Commission of India, which was established in 1950.
 
• The First Five-Year Plan (1951-1956) focused on the agricultural sector, aiming to overcome food shortages and improve living standards.
 
 
 
• **Planning Commission**
 
 
• The Planning Commission was an institution in the Government of India which formulated India's Five-Year Plans, among other functions.
 
• It was established in 1950 by a Cabinet resolution under the advice of the first Prime Minister, Jawaharlal Nehru.
 
• The Commission was tasked with assessing the country's resources and formulating plans for the most effective and balanced utilization of resources.
 
• In 2014, the Planning Commission was replaced by the NITI Aayog (National Institution for Transforming India) by the Narendra Modi government.
 
 
 
• **Objectives of the Five-Year Plans**
 
 
• The primary objectives were to increase national income, achieve full employment, reduce inequalities of income and wealth, and establish a socialist pattern of society.
 
• Other specific objectives included reducing poverty, improving infrastructure, and enhancing the quality of life for Indian citizens.
 
 
 
• **Significance of the Five-Year Plans**
 
 
• The Five-Year Plans were instrumental in transforming India's economy from an agrarian base to a more diversified one with a substantial industrial sector.
 
• They laid the foundation for modern economic development and contributed to significant improvements in various economic indicators, such as GDP growth and poverty reduction.
 
• The plans also played a critical role in establishing and expanding public sector enterprises and infrastructure development across the country.

questions.question: What was the target growth rate of the Indian economy in the second five-year plan?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__4.5%__**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The second five-year plan, **spanning from **1956 to 1961, **aimed for a **target growth rate **of** 4.5% **for the Indian economy.
 
• However, the actual growth rate fell slightly short at **4.27%**.
 
• **Drafted by P.C. Mahalanobis**, this plan prioritized rapid industrialization and the development of the public sector, with an emphasis on achieving quick structural transformation.
 
• To protect domestic industries, the government implemented tariffs on imports, while also allocating nearly 50 billion rupees across various sectors to meet set targets.
 
• Additionally, the plan advocated for the adoption of new technology and efficient investments to propel India's annual national income growth.
 
• Despite its objectives, the second five-year plan faced criticism from classical liberal economist **B.R. Shenoy**.
 
• He argued that the plan's heavy reliance on deficit financing to promote industrialization posed significant risks and could potentially lead to economic instability.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The Second Five-Year Plan** placed a significant emphasis on the development of the public sector and aimed for **"rapid industrialization."**
 
• This plan was guided by the **Mahalanobis model,** an economic development framework devised by Indian statistician Prasanta Chandra Mahalanobis in 1953.
 
• At the core of the plan was the objective of determining the optimal allocation of investment across various productive sectors to achieve maximum long-term economic growth.
 
• To achieve this, the plan utilized state-of-the-art techniques of operations research and optimization, along with innovative applications of statistical models developed at the Indian Statistical Institute.
